notes: The phrase the heads of the tribes writes two the's; read under rule 29's arthrous case, the article on maṭṭôṯ takes the one standing before its own word and the construct rāʾšēy a supplied one, so nothing is fronted.
Three of's are counted against the morphemes that license them: the construct relation of rāʾšēy→maṭṭôṯ, the written lamed of libnēy, and the construct relation of bənēy→yiśrāʾēl (rules 11 and 19).
zeh haddābār is read with the demonstrative as subject and haddābār as predicate, so the copula joins the noun under rule 20 while the article takes the written the.
